PullRequest.Title: menus: auto-select the first enabled action in native context menus
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to [#346082](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/346082) that addresses its [review comment](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/346082#discussion_r4471320713).

Native context menus show a group's title as a disabled item at the start of the group. With `autoSelectItem: true` and a titled first group, `NativeContextMenuService` ([contextmenuService.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/54eee47777c2485d21638845eed6235db0942eb2/src/vs/workbench/services/contextmenu/electron-browser/contextmenuService.ts)) passed `positioningItem: 0`, which targets that title instead of the first action.

## Changes

- With `autoSelectItem: true`, native context menus position the first item that is neither a separator nor disabled, or no item if there is none. This matches the custom menu, whose `ActionBar.focus(true)` focuses the first enabled item and so skips separators and headers, and the `autoSelectItem` documentation ("`true` focuses the first enabled action").
- Numeric selections are unchanged: they still map past the inserted titles to the selected action.
- This also changes untitled menus: a menu whose first action is disabled now positions the first enabled action instead of the disabled one, as the custom menu already does.

## Impact

Electron only applies `positioningItem` on macOS, where it places that item under the mouse cursor, and native context menus are opt-in (`window.menuStyle` follows the title bar style, which defaults to custom). No shipped menu hits the titled case: only the three Canvas menus titled in [#346082](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/346082) have group titles, and none of them is shown with `autoSelectItem: true`. This fixes a latent bug in the new API.

## How to test

The titled-menu test in [contextmenuService.test.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/54eee47777c2485d21638845eed6235db0942eb2/src/vs/workbench/services/contextmenu/test/electron-browser/contextmenuService.test.ts) now also shows its menu with `autoSelectItem: true` and expects item 1, the first action after the "Recent" title. Without the fix it fails with `positioningItems: [0, 4]` instead of `[1, 4]`. Not tested manually, since no shipped menu combines group titles with `autoSelectItem: true`.

Validation on the head of this PR (`54eee47777c`):
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/contextmenu/test/electron-browser/contextmenuService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/contextview/test/browser/contextMenuHandler.test.ts`: 39 passing
- The same `contextmenuService.test.ts` run with the production change reverted: 1 failing (the titled-menu test, as described above)
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run eslint` on the 2 changed files: passed

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an opt-in native context menu with autoSelectItem=true, including menus whose first group has a title or disabled actions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On user invocation, actions are synchronously transformed into native menu items, the changed findIndex scans top-level items until the first enabled non-separator, then popup serializes the menu and sends one renderer-to-main IPC before Electron displays it. The scan is on the critical path but is bounded by the already-materialized top-level menu.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serializes the complete native menu and sends CONTEXT_MENU_CHANNEL from the renderer to Electron's main process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one IPC send per native context-menu opening, regardless of item count; payload size remains proportional to the complete menu including nested submenus.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same popup call serialized the same menu and sent one IPC; only positioningItem computation was previously constant-time for boolean true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The IPC is required to display the native menu and remains after the synchronous selection scan.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Top-level native menu item count after group-title insertion. The added work is O(n) worst case only when all or most top-level entries are separators/disabled; ordinary menus stop at the first enabled action. Existing createMenu and popup serialization already perform O(n), or O(total nested items), work for the same invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous menu-building/selection pass and one IPC send per user-triggered menu opening; the diff adds no parallel tasks, queue, subprocess, or aggregate concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates before or after the change. Every menu opening rebuilds and serializes its current actions; the changed selection scan neither adds cache misses nor defeats coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed O(n) scan and critical-path placement from the production hunk and popup call path; high confidence that it adds no IPC, filesystem, network, database, or subprocess operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact menu sizes and opening frequency vary, but known auto-select callers construct small choice/action menus. Even for a large menu, the new top-level scan is dominated by existing menu construction and full serialization and does not change boundary count or asymptotic complexity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added scan is one allocation-free linear pass over an array already created and then fully serialized on the same invocation, usually terminating at the first enabled item; it neither changes asymptotic cost nor boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a native context menu with numeric autoSelectItem, or with auto-selection disabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Menu construction and the existing single popup IPC remain on the display critical path. The changed findIndex branch is not executed for numeric, false, or undefined selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serializes and sends the native menu to the main process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical menu serialization and one IPC send per opening.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Menu action/item count controls existing construction and serialization only; the diff adds no item-scaled work in this scenario.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous menu construction and one IPC send per invocation, unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; behavior is unchanged for cold and repeated openings.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the explicit typeof/boolean branch in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to the diff because the new scan branch is unreachable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change for this scenario.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced native context-menu opening through action transformation, menu construction, selection, serialization, and renderer-to-main IPC. The production change adds only a bounded top-level findIndex for boolean auto-selection; it introduces no expensive boundary, concurrency, retained state, or new asymptotic cost relative to existing full menu construction and serialization. No valid performance findings and no regression-fix learning signal.
